# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination
**Member:** Reese Iverson
**Member ID:** W233165693
**Reference number:** POC-757C3B7E16-21498
**Date of denial notice:** August 6, 2026
**Service denied:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Ordering surgeon:** Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery
**Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery 2025-11-15 (HTML), effective 2025-11-15 — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), which Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana denied on August 6, 2026 under reference number POC-757C3B7E16-21498. The notice states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records in my file document a course of conservative care that meets the plan's own published requirements.

I am writing about the criteria in the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline dated 2025-11-15, which is the guideline my plan uses for musculoskeletal surgery and which Carelon publishes publicly at the address above. Below I quote that guideline's language and match each requirement to what my medical records show.

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

**The plan's conservative care requirement.** The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management"

My records document 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy, from February 24, 2026 to June 16, 2026, with 16 visits completed, focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. That is documented in my physical therapy discharge note. My pain continued despite completing that course.

**What conservative management must include.** The guideline states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My care included physical therapy as described above, plus more than one complementary treatment: NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on March 30, 2026 that gave only about three weeks of partial relief.

**Completion of the full course.** The guideline states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

I completed my physical therapy course through discharge on June 16, 2026. This was all for the current episode of shoulder pain, not a separate or older problem.

**Documentation of compliance.** The guideline states:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My attendance and progress are documented in the physical therapy discharge note covering all 16 visits, and my medication trial and injection are documented in my chart. If any of these records were not in the packet the reviewer saw, I ask that they be requested and reviewed before a decision is finalized.

**Duration of symptoms and how they began.** The guideline states:

> "Gradual onset of shoulder pain in the absence of a significant traumatic event within the preceding 3 months"

and

> "Symptoms are present for at least 3 months"

My records describe 18 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest. There is no traumatic injury in my history.

**Pain and its effect on daily life.** The guideline states:

> "Pain ≥ 3 on the VAS scale which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living"

My records document that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. My recorded pain score is at [VAS pain score as documented in the office notes — to be supplied from the chart].

**Physical examination.** The guideline states:

> "Physical exam consistent with symptomatic rotator cuff tear (e.g., drop arm test, painful arc, full/empty can test, weakness of internal/external rotation or abduction)"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**Imaging.** The guideline states:

> "Recent advanced imaging confirms features of a degenerative full thickness tear"

and separately:

> "Imaging report . The provider shall submit a detailed imaging report for studies obtained within the past 12 months. In the absence of a detailed report, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

An MRI of my shoulder on July 7, 2026 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. That study is well within the past 12 months, and the report is available for the reviewer.

**Tobacco.** The guideline states:

> "For primary rotator cuff repair, adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco and nicotine products for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended."

I am a non-smoker, as documented in my chart. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## A note about the criteria list

The guideline's introduction to the acute full-thickness tear pathway reads:

> "Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary for an acute full thickness tear when ALL the following criteria are met:"

That sentence introduces a list of further conditions, and the policy contains additional criteria that I have not reproduced here. My tear is not described in my records as traumatic or acute, so I believe the degenerative full-thickness tear criteria are the ones that apply to me, and I have addressed those above. I am not in a position to know which specific criteria the reviewer applied.

## Request for the criteria the plan used

I am asking Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Louisiana to send me, in writing, the specific clinical criteria that were applied to my request, including the exact provision the reviewer found unmet and the name and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination. The plan and its review vendor hold those criteria; I do not. Carelon publishes its Joint Surgery, Spine Surgery and Small Joint Surgery guidelines publicly and without a login, so identifying the guideline and provision applied to my case should be straightforward. Without that information I cannot fully respond to the reason given for the denial.

## What I am asking for

Please reconsider and overturn the denial of CPT 29827 and authorize the rotator cuff repair recommended by Dr. Duval, who has documented in my chart that this procedure is medically necessary for me. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, please send me a written explanation that identifies the exact criterion not met and tells me how to request the next level of review, including external review.

I understand my appeal must be received by February 2, 2027, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; any member who is unsure where to send an appeal can call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at my records.

Sincerely,

**Reese Iverson**
Member ID: W233165693
Reference number: POC-757C3B7E16-21498
